releaseNote.summary: A flow can pin its default version in sys-version-registry; floating requests stay at or below it and newer versions stay pending until an explicit request.

flowDefaultVersion.description: Publish != Activate. A flow's default-version pointer lives in the sys-version-registry system flow (instance key = flow key, data {type:'Flow', defaultVersion: 'M'|'M.m'|'M.m.p'|'M.m.p-pkg.x.y.z'|null, reason?}; 'latest' and blank are rejected, type is informational). With a pointer P, the effective default D is the best published match of P: null/empty/latest requests resolve to D, 'M' / 'M.m' requests resolve to the best match at or below D, and versions above D stay pending - reachable only by an explicit full ('-pkg.') or artifact ('2.2.0') request. A request that only matches pending versions answers Instance:100051 (404); a pointer that matches no published version answers Instance:100052 (409) and fails closed (it also blocks explicit artifact requests while broken; full versions still work). An unreadable registry answers Instance:100053 (503, transient, never negative-cached). Flows without a registry instance, sys-* flows and domains whose core package has no registry flow keep today's behaviour exactly. A pointer change invalidates the flow's resolution through a best-effort post-commit job (generation bump, at most ~5 s cross-pod propagation); writes to the registry flow are validated before admission (Instance:100052, the registry instance stays Active). SubFlow correlation stores the child's resolved version. Telemetry: Instance.Create span tag vnext.flow.version.requested; cache span tags vnext.flow.version.pointer / .source (automatic|explicit|default|ceiling). Requires the vnext-sys-flow package that ships sys-version-registry; an older package behaves as Automatic.
